movie.title: The Ugly Stepsister
movie.overview: In a fairy-tale kingdom where beauty is a brutal business, Elvira battles to compete with her incredibly beautiful stepsister, Agnes, and she will go to any length to catch the Prince’s eye.

reviews.author: CinemaSerf
reviews.content: Now I don’t suppose you’d have kicked “Prince Julian” (Isac Calmroth) out of bed for eating herring, but right from the start this apple of everyone’s eye looks distinctly dull! I’m not sure that the besotted “Elvira” (Lea Myren) realised that when she embarked on quite a tortuous make-over to turn her chubby and buck-toothed body into something that might turn the head of this royal highness, but needs must when the debt collectors are circling. This is probably the most grotesque take on the “Cinderella” story you are ever like to see, as it pretty graphically shows the life of this young girl, her stepsister, her mother and her downright cruel Svengali who thinks nothing of stitching her eyelids on or rearranging her teeth - without, of course, any anaesthetic. Where this also drifts away from the more traditional approach is the venality of the whole thing. “Elvira” is certainly a victim of greed, but it’s more a sort of uneducated and vulgar kind from her guardian rather than anything more spiteful or hateful. Moot point? Well, not really as in the end it is actually quite difficult to actually loathe this family desperate to climb the silky pole. I almost felt sorry for all of them. It’s gory, there’s a fair smattering of sex and our princeling can even turn his hand to poetry - though not the stuff that Yeats might have to worry about. The production has been eerily and effectively crafted with plenty of detail in the settings and costumes, and the overall message of style over substance and social and sexual conformity is writ large throughout. It turns out that there are more ways than one to get your foot in that slipper, and not all of this will be for the squeamish. I enjoyed this dark, occasionally comedic and poignant look at just what we’ll do to for love, lust and lucre.

reviews.author: Sierbahnn
reviews.content:
Fairytale body-horror
This is a GRIM take on Cinderella, and very very ... ew. Not for the feint of heart, but if you came for the bodyhorror then you shall not be disappointed.

The setting for this is lovely, the acting appropriate, the direction works, and the score is messing with you constantly. All and all this is a great adaptation, and shows a very dark side to this tale. Well worth a watch!

reviews.author: Alunauwie
reviews.content:
*The Ugly Stepsister* offers a compelling reinterpretation of the Cinderella story by exploring themes of love, obsession, and unrealistic beauty standards through strong character motivations, unsettling visuals, and powerful performances. Although a few supporting characters lack deeper development and some plot points feel inconsistent, the film delivers an emotionally resonant journey with thought-provoking social commentary. Overall, it is a distinctive and rewarding dark fairy tale that is easy to recommend for viewers looking for a fresh and mature take on a familiar classic.

BY ALUNAUWIE

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: In a kingdom where physical appearance dictates worth, Elvira goes to terrifying lengths to outshine her stunning stepsister Agnes and capture the Prince's affection.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: Set in a ruthless fairy-tale world where beauty is the ultimate currency, Elvira struggles under the shadow of her impossibly gorgeous stepsister, Agnes. Driven by envy and societal pressure, Elvira sets her sights on winning the royal Prince's heart at any cost. As competition escalates, her desperate ambition draws her into dark and gruesome territory. Ultimately, Elvira demonstrates just how far she is willing to alter herself and manipulate those around her to achieve her twisted idea of happily ever after.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: In a realm where physical beauty strictly defines social status and power, Elvira endures constant comparison to her breathtaking stepsister, Agnes. When the kingdom announces a grand ball where the Prince will select his bride, the competitive pressure within the household reaches a boiling point. Unwilling to accept her status as the overlooked stepsister, Elvira embarks on a dark journey to transform her appearance and outmaneuver Agnes. Her quest rapidly devolves into extreme measures, blending body horror with dark comedy as she subjects herself to painful rituals and desperate schemes. Meanwhile, Agnes navigates her own struggles under the oppressive expectations of perfection imposed by their society. As the night of the royal ball approaches, Elvira's fixation with the Prince turns into an dangerous obsession that threatens to destroy everyone involved. The narrative subverts traditional fairy-tale tropes by exploring the horrifying extremes people will go to for external validation. Ultimately, Elvira's relentless pursuit of royal favor culminates in a dramatic showdown that exposes the true, ugly cost of beauty.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: In a kingdom where beauty is a brutal and high-stakes business, Elvira lives in the overwhelming shadow of her exceptionally gorgeous stepsister, Agnes. When the royal family announces a search for the Prince's future bride, Elvira becomes determined to break free from her role as the overlooked stepsister and secure the Prince's hand. Blending elements of horror, drama, and dark comedy, the story follows Elvira's increasingly drastic and dangerous efforts to compete with Agnes and catch the Prince's eye. As social pressures mount and obsession takes over, the tale offers a dark, satirical reimagining of classic fairy-tale tropes, examining the terrifying lengths to which one will go in the pursuit of perfection and status.
